title: Laboratory Equipment & Position
pedagogicalStatus: Unreviewed draft: formative practice only; CEFR mastery disabled.

sources.title: The first laboratory bench (learning)
paragraphs: In this beginner lesson, all equipment is disconnected and used only for naming and position practice. On the worktable, there is one meterstick and there are two timers. The digital scale is next to the meterstick. A notebook is between the two timers. A plastic tray is behind the notebook. Under the worktable is an empty equipment box.

Maya says, “This is my notebook. These are our timers.” She points across the classroom: “That is the instructor’s cart. Those are the extra rulers.” Nothing in this text requires students to connect or energize electrical equipment.

sources.title: A classroom inventory (learning)
paragraphs:
| Label | Item | Number | Location |
|---|---|---:|---|
| A | meterstick | 1 | on the left shelf |
| B | timer | 2 | on the middle shelf |
| C | digital scale | 1 | on the right shelf |
| D | plastic tray | 1 | under the middle shelf |
| E | notebook | 3 | in the cabinet |
| F | thermometer | 1 | in the drawer |

These labels describe a fictional teaching room, not an inventory at USTHB. An ammeter measures electric current; a voltmeter measures voltage. A thermometer measures temperature; a meterstick measures length. This is identification practice only.

sources.title: Setup instructions on a paper worksheet (learning)
paragraphs: This task uses cards with equipment pictures, not working electrical apparatus.

First, put the *timer* card in the center of the desk outline. Next, place the *ruler* card to the left of the timer. Then put the *scale* card to the right of the timer. Finally, draw a notebook below the timer. The words left and right describe the worksheet as you face it; the front edge is at the bottom. Check the labels before you finish.

sources.title: Two students describe a layout (learning)
paragraphs:
**Lena:** Is there a ruler next to the tray?
**Noah:** Yes, there is. The ruler is on the left of the tray.
**Lena:** Are there three timers on this desk?
**Noah:** No, there aren't. There are two timers. One is near us and the other is across the desk.
**Lena:** Is the notebook between them?
**Noah:** Yes. First we check the labels, then we copy the positions, and finally we compare our drawings.
“Near us” and “across the desk” depend on the speakers’ positions. Such expressions are never used for machine-scored position questions without an explicit viewpoint.
